Definition: from G2532 and G4007; and indeed, i.e. nevertheless or notwithstanding:--and yet, although.
BiblicalUsage: Kaiper is 'and indeed' or 'though' — the word that concedes a point and then presses past it. Though He were a Son, yet learned He obedience by the things which He suffered; Esau found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears; and Peter will put the saints always in remembrance, though they know the truth already.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word teaches me to hold two truths at once: Christ learned obedience though He was the Son, and I must be reminded though I already know.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
